title: Derivative equals singleton Fourier coefficient
statement: Let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional sign cube to $\{\pm1\}$, and suppose the sum of the squared Fourier coefficients of its real-valued version over all singleton subsets is $1$. Then, for every coordinate $i$ and every cube point $x$, the discrete derivative of the real-valued version of $f$ in coordinate $i$ at $x$ equals its Fourier coefficient on the singleton $\{i\}$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
